FAILING ENDPOINT
  GET /bug/polymorphic-v2?type=GUEST&userId=u789

  GUEST users should receive restricted read-only access.
  Expected profile: permissions=[read:public]

OBSERVED
  HTTP 200 returned. The profile contains elevated permissions.
  Observed: permissions=[read,write,delete,manage,admin]
  GUEST users have full administrator permissions — privilege escalation.

No exception. The response is structurally valid JSON.

The server log confirms the route was dispatched, but does not identify which
implementation handled the request.

Investigate the root cause. The application source is in:
  src/main/java/com/example/demo/

Found it. `GuestHandler.handle()` at line 13 returns `permissions=[read,write,delete,manage,admin]` — full admin permissions — instead of the restricted `permissions=[read:public]` that GUEST users should receive.

Thought: The bug is in `GuestHandler.java` line 13. The `handle()` method returns a profile with full admin permissions `[read,write,delete,manage,admin]` instead of the restricted guest permissions `[read:public]`. The router correctly dispatches to `GuestHandler` via polymorphic dispatch on the `RequestHandlerV2` interface, but `GuestHandler` itself has the wrong permission set hardcoded.

**Root cause:** `bug3v2/GuestHandler.java` line 13.

The `GuestHandler.handle()` method has the wrong permissions hardcoded — it returns `permissions=[read,write,delete,manage,admin]` (full admin access) when it should return `permissions=[read:public]` (restricted read-only).

**Fix:**
```java
// Before (line 13):
return "PROFILE:{userId=" + request.userId() + ",role=guest,permissions=[read,write,delete,manage,admin]}";

// After:
return "PROFILE:{userId=" + request.userId() + ",role=guest,permissions=[read:public]}";
```

The router (`RequestRouter2`) correctly dispatches `GUEST` requests to `GuestHandler` via polymorphic interface dispatch — the bug is entirely within the handler's return value, not the routing logic.
